note: `#js` HAS AN EVALUATED PAYLOAD, EXCEPT FOR ITS KEYS. ClojureScript compiles `#js {:year (.year a-date)}` to a JavaScript object LITERAL, and a literal's VALUES are evaluated; the blanket "payloads are data either way" rule dropped every call and member access in the values, six real ones in metabase's util/time/impl.cljs:313-319 alone. The discriminator is the TAG: `#js` (and the historical `#JS`) is the one tag whose payload is a literal with evaluated values, while `#inst`, `#uuid` and every record/class literal take DATA. The KEYS are still data — a key is a property name, not an expression — so a map walks its values and a vector walks its elements. `String/valueOf` and `Integer/parseInt` are namespace-qualified CALLS (no dot on either side of the slash) and must appear as calls inside the vector. `str/join` and `File/listFiles` stand in for the interop statics: `String/valueOf` and `Integer/parseInt` are among the 69 uncurried interop statics the core list DECLARES, so they are suppressed as builtins and would emit nothing inside a `#js` payload too — a fixture written with them would pass whether or not the payload were walked.
